ing: wiri wiri or scotch bonnet chili
st: Put the beef in a large heavy pot with the onion, garlic, cinnamon, cloves, thyme, orange peel and [[2 tsp]] salt.
Pour in [[0.5 cup]] cassareep and [[6 cups]] water. Add the whole chilies and [[2 tbsp]] brown sugar.
Bring to a boil, skim any foam, then lower to the lowest simmer.
Cover and simmer for 2 hours 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the meat is very tender.
Taste the sauce. It should be dark, a little bitter-sweet and savory. Add salt or sugar if needed.
Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes to thicken it slightly. Remove the cinnamon, orange peel, thyme stems and chilies.
Cool and reheat the next day if you can, since the flavor deepens. Serve hot with bread or rice.
Season the chicken with [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large heavy pot and brown the chicken for 8 minutes. Add the onion and garlic and cook 4 minutes.
Drain the soaked peas and add them to the pot with [[4 cups]] water, the thyme and the chili. Boil, then simmer covered for 35 minutes until the peas begin to soften.
Pour in the coconut milk and [[1 tsp]] salt, and bring back to a boil.
Stir in the rinsed rice and scallions. The liquid should sit about 1 inch above the rice; add a splash of water if not.
Cover tightly, turn the heat to the lowest setting and cook for 20 minutes without lifting the lid.
Rest off the heat for 10 minutes. Check the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Remove the thyme stems and chili, fluff with a fork and serve.
Soak the salt cod in cold water overnight, changing the water twice. Drain, flake it and remove any bones.
Mix the flour with [[0.5 tsp]] salt, then stir in about [[0.5 cup]] water to make a firm dough. Roll small pieces into finger-shaped dumplings.
In a large pot combine [[4 cups]] water, the coconut milk, onion, garlic, scallions, thyme and whole chili. Bring to a boil.
Add the cassava and sweet potato. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the plantains, salt cod and [[1 tsp]] salt. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Drop in the dumplings. Cover and cook for 20 minutes until they are firm and cooked through and the sauce is thick.
Remove the chili and thyme stems. Taste and adjust the salt. Serve hot.
Mix the curry powder with a splash of water to make a paste. Rub half of it with [[1 tsp]] salt into the chicken and rest 20 minutes.
Heat [[0.25 cup]] oil in a large pot. Fry the onions and garlic for 5 minutes, then add the rest of the curry paste and cumin. Cook 3 minutes until fragrant and thick.
Add the chicken and stir to coat. Cook 8 minutes.
Add the potatoes, thyme, chili, [[2 cups]] water and [[1 tsp]] salt. Cover and simmer for 35 minutes until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C) and the potatoes are soft.
For the roti, mix [[3 cups]] flour, baking powder and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Stir in about [[1 cup]] warm water and knead 5 minutes into a soft dough. Cover and rest 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into 6 balls. Roll each into a thin round about 8 inches wide and brush with oil. Cook in a hot dry skillet for 1 to 2 minutes per side, brushing with a little of the roti oil.
Clap or crumple the cooked roti in a towel to soften it.
Serve the curry with the roti torn into pieces for scooping.
Boil the split peas in [[4 cups]] water with the garlic and turmeric for 40 minutes until very soft. Drain well.
Cool the peas, then grind them to a fine, dry crumb with the cumin and [[1 tsp]] salt in a food processor.
Mix the flour, baking powder and [[1 tsp]] salt. Add the warm water slowly and knead 5 minutes to a soft, smooth dough. Cover and rest 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into 8 balls. Flatten one, put 2 tablespoons of the pea mix in the middle and pinch the edges closed over it.
Roll the filled ball gently into a thin round about 8 inches wide, without letting the filling break through.
Cook in a hot dry skillet over medium heat for 1 minute per side. Brush with a little of the oil and flip twice more until blistered and golden.
Wrap the cooked puri in a clean towel to keep them soft. Serve with curry.
Crush the garlic with [[1 tsp]] salt into a rough paste. Mix with [[1 cup]] vinegar, the thyme leaves, chilies, pepper and sugar.
Add the pork and onion and stir well. Cover and marinate in the fridge for at least [[24 hours]] (traditionally a few days).
Lift the pork out of the marinade, keeping the marinade.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a heavy pot and brown the pork in batches for about 8 minutes, until golden on all sides.
Add the marinade and [[1 cup]] water, plus [[1 tsp]] salt. Bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer on low for 1 hour 15 minutes, until the pork is tender and has reached at least 145°F (63°C).
Uncover and cook 10 minutes more to reduce the sauce. Serve with bread or rice.

ing: dried, or fresh chow mein noodles
st: Toss the chicken with [[2 tbsp]] soy sauce, the ginger and pepper. Let it sit 15 minutes.
Boil the noodles in salted water according to the package until just tender. Drain, rinse with cold water and toss with the sesame oil.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat. Stir-fry the chicken for 5 minutes until it reaches 165°F (74°C). Set aside.
Add [[1 tbsp]] oil. Stir-fry the onion, carrots and garlic for 3 minutes.
Add the cabbage and stir-fry for 2 minutes until just wilted.
Add the last [[1 tbsp]] oil, then the noodles, the chicken, [[2 tbsp]] soy sauce and the salt. Toss for 3 minutes until everything is hot.
Mix in the scallions and serve right away.

ing: finely minced, or 0.5 tsp hot sauce
st: Mix the flour, baking powder and salt in a bowl. Rub in the cold butter with your fingertips until it looks like coarse crumbs.
Add about [[0.33 cup]] cold water a spoonful at a time and press into a smooth dough. Wrap and chill for [[30 minutes]].
Mix the cheese with the chili and mustard in a bowl until it forms a rough paste.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Roll the dough into a rectangle about 12x8 inches and 0.125 inch thick.
Cut the dough into 12 strips. Put a spoonful of cheese along each strip, then roll up and seal with a dab of water.
Place on a lined tray, seam side down, and brush with the beaten egg.
Bake for 25 minutes until puffed and golden brown. Cool 5 minutes before eating.
Cook the pineapple with [[0.5 cup]] sugar, the cinnamon and lemon juice in a pan over medium-low heat for 25 minutes, stirring, until thick like jam. Cool.
Mix the flour, powdered sugar and salt. Rub in the butter to coarse crumbs.
Add about [[0.25 cup]] cold water a spoonful at a time and press into a smooth dough. Chill for [[30 minutes]].
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Roll the dough 0.125 inch thick and cut into 3-inch circles.
Put a spoonful of pineapple jam in the center of each circle.
Fold up the sides to make a triangle, pinching the three corners and leaving the center open.
Place on a lined tray and brush the pastry with beaten egg.
Bake for 20 minutes until golden. Cool on a rack.

ing: or use cherry juice for an alcohol-free version
st: The day before, chop the fruit small or pulse in a food processor to a chunky paste. Soak it in [[1 cup]] rum (or cherry juice) in a covered jar for at least [[24 hours]].
Heat the oven to 300°F (150°C). Line a 9-inch round pan with parchment and grease it.
Cream the butter and sugar for 5 minutes until pale and fluffy.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla, lime zest and burnt sugar or molasses until the batter is dark.
Whisk together the flour, baking powder, cinnamon, nutmeg and salt. Fold into the batter.
Fold in the soaked fruit with all its liquid until even.
Pour into the pan and bake for 2 hours 15 minutes, until a skewer in the center comes out clean. Cover loosely with foil if it browns too fast.
While hot, poke holes with a skewer and brush with the remaining [[0.5 cup]] rum or juice.
Cool completely in the pan. Wrap and rest overnight before slicing.
